summary: Valve's class-based multiplayer shooter lineage, from the original Quake mod through Team Fortress Classic and Team Fortress 2.

entries.title: Team Fortress

emulation.notes: Use a modern Quake/QuakeWorld source port or FortressOne-style preservation route.

primary.why: The original Team Fortress is a Quake mod; Windows with a modern Quake/QuakeWorld setup is the easiest preservation route while Linux and macOS remain possible through compatible engines.
primary.how_to_play: Install Quake/QuakeWorld legally, add the Team Fortress mod files, and use a modern source port or preservation fork such as FortressOne if vanilla setup is impractical.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate the original mod with Team Fortress Classic or Team Fortress 2.

entries.title: Team Fortress Classic

primary.why: Team Fortress Classic shipped on Windows and later supported OS X and Linux; Windows remains the best-supported current Steam route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Steam Windows release, preserving server/browser state and any community server details.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mac compatibility is limited on modern macOS; document community server dependencies.

entries.title: Team Fortress 2

primary.why: Team Fortress 2 launched on Windows, Xbox 360, and PS3, later adding macOS and Linux; the actively updated Windows Steam client is the definitive current route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Steam Windows client; document the update, server type, and item/account state because the game is a long-running live service.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service state, item economy, and server environment matter; document date and update.
